name: Agra Petha & Mughlai Cuisine
description: Translucent soft candy made from ash gourd (winter melon), perfected during Mughal emperor Shah Jahan's reign, alongside rich slow-cooked Mughlai dum curries.
cultural_significance: Traditional confectionery perfected by royal confectioners in Tajganj; holds GI-recognition advocacy.

name: Jaipur Blue Pottery
description: Turquoise-glazed quartz pottery with Persian and Central Asian design influences, uniquely made without clay using ground quartz stone, glass, and natural gums.
cultural_significance: Geographical Indication (GI) tagged traditional art form revived under Maharaja Sawai Ram Singh II in the 19th century.

name: Mumbai Vada Pav & Coastal Malvani Cuisine
description: The quintessential culinary pulse of Mumbai: spiced potato fritters in pav bread with garlic chutney, alongside fresh Konkan coastal fish curries infused with kokum and coconut.
cultural_significance: Pioneered in 1966 outside Dadar railway station, representing the working-class spirit and community resilience of Mumbai.

name: Banarasi Zari Silk Weaving
description: Opulent handloom silk brocades woven with genuine gold and silver electroplated zari threads, featuring intricate Mughal-inspired floral jaal and paisley motifs.
cultural_significance: UNESCO and GI-protected heritage craft practiced by master weavers (karigars) for over six centuries along the ghats.

name: Kathakali Classical Dance-Drama & Spices
description: Vibrant storytelling dance-theatre with elaborate face makeup (chutti), sacred mudras, and traditional percussion, paired with ancient spice trading traditions of Malabar pepper and cardamom.
cultural_significance: Recognized intangible cultural heritage rooted in temple traditions and centuries of international maritime exchange.

name: Old Delhi Culinary & Zardozi Heritage
description: Shahjahanabad's historic culinary lanes (Paranthe Wali Gali, Karim's) intertwined with Kinari Bazaar's silver tinsel and 300-year-old heavy gold zardozi embroidery ateliers.
cultural_significance: Historical street market designed in 1650 by Princess Jahanara Begum, reflecting living Mughal and Delhi Sultanate traditions.

name: Durga Puja & Bengali Sweets (Rosogolla, Sandesh)
description: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity festival celebrating feminine divine power with monumental art pandals, coupled with historic cottage cheese sweet confections.
cultural_significance: UNESCO inscribed festival in 2021 as a public celebration of art, religion, social harmony, and artisan craftsmanship.

name: Carnatic Classical Music & Kanchipuram Weaving
description: UNESCO Creative Cities Network designation for Music, showcasing Margazhi Music Season kutcheris, Bharatanatyam dance academies, and pure mulberry silk Kanchipuram sarees.
cultural_significance: Over a millennium of temple arts, literary Sangam heritage, and south Indian classical music preservation.
